note: Written by a Claude Code session working on this repo, for whichever agent picks this up next -- not runtime telemetry, a findings summary.
summary: This session (1) optimized fried.js's runtime, (2) found and fixed 3 real bugs in patcher.js via adversarial testing, (3) worked a 7-item improvement backlog end to end, dogfooding the patcher throughout and extending it (removeStatement) when it hit a real capability gap, (4) then patcher.js was overwritten externally -- by the user's account, another agent working on a parallel copy at ~/Downloads/fried-app-copy/fried-app copy/src/patcher.js -- and that overwrite reintroduced 2 of the 3 bugs this session had fixed, plus broke 2 of this session's own removeStatement tests.

failingTests.name: patcher.js: setProp() throws instead of silently editing the wrong node when a key is duplicated
failingTests.cause: REGRESSION. findUiCallsByKey() was reverted to `found.set(key, node)` (last-write-wins, one node per key) instead of tracking an array per key. requireUiNode() no longer checks nodes.length > 1. Confirmed bug this session: two ui(...) calls sharing a `key` cause setProp/setChildText/addChild to silently edit whichever call the Map happened to keep, with no warning -- an AI agent addressing 'the element with key x' gets no signal it hit the wrong one.

failingTests.name: patcher.js: removeChild() throws instead of silently removing the wrong child when a child key is duplicated
failingTests.cause: Same root cause as above, in removeChild()'s own separate child-key scan (not routed through findUiCallsByKey, has its own copy of the same bug).

failingTests.name: patcher.js: removeStatement() removes an exported function declaration
failingTests.cause: External removeStatement() throws 'no top-level const or function named "greet" found' for `export function greet() {...}` -- its ExportNamedDeclaration handling doesn't match this session's version. Needs reconciling, not just reverting: the external version added useful things (see below) that shouldn't be thrown away to fix this.

failingTests.name: patcher.js: removeStatement() refuses a multi-declarator statement rather than guess
failingTests.cause: External removeStatement() no longer throws for `let a, b, c;` when asked to remove `b` -- this session's version deliberately refuses (removing the whole statement would silently delete a and c too). Need to check what the external version actually does in this case; if it silently removes the whole statement or guesses, that's a correctness risk worth fixing before this ships.

friedJsState.note: fried.js itself was NOT touched by the external change -- only patcher.js was overwritten. All this session's runtime work (prefix/suffix fast-path diffing, event-handler tests, mount/unmount thrashing, etc.) is intact and verified.

externalChangeWorthKeeping.description: The version that overwrote patcher.js also added real value this session didn't have: Levenshtein-based 'nearest match' suggestions on failed lookups (requireUiNode, presumably others), a batch-patching entry point, and a validate() that returns structured {line, column, pos} instead of just a message string. These look genuinely useful and worth reconciling INTO the codebase, not discarding to fix the regressions above.
externalChangeWorthKeeping.recommendation: Whoever picks this up: reconcile rather than choose one side wholesale. Keep the nearest-match/structured-validate/batch additions. Restore the array-per-key duplicate-key check in findUiCallsByKey/requireUiNode (and removeChild's own copy of that scan) that the external version dropped. Reconcile removeStatement's exported-function and multi-declarator handling -- re-run this session's test.js (specifically the 4 failing tests listed above) as the acceptance check once done.
